title: Precision Sandbox Decision Lab - Optimize Console Walkthrough
summary: Redwood AE/SE ran an interactive Optimize console demo focused on choosing precision profiles for Cedar Analytics' low-latency inference use case. Discussed INT8 and FP8 tradeoffs, automated fallback heuristics, sandbox benchmarking steps, and enterprise controls (KMS, audit logs). Agreed next steps: grant sandbox, share sensitivity spreadsheet, and schedule a 2-hour hands-on benchmark with Cedar's sample prompts.
action_items: Ethan Morales: Share INT8/FP8 sensitivity spreadsheet and recent benchmark CSV - due 2026-10-20
Priya Shah: Provision Optimize sandbox workspace with Cedar sample dataset and default qprofiles - due 2026-10-21
Liam O'Neill: Provide 500 representative prompts and target latency SLOs - due 2026-10-22
next_steps: Ethan to send sandbox invite + instructions
Run 2-hour hybrid-precision sweep in sandbox (AE+SE assisted)
Follow-up call to review results and select production profile
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-18 | 15:00 PT | Duration 62m | Attendees: Ethan Morales (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jonas Kline (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Cedar CTO), Liam O'Neill (ML Eng), Rosa Martínez (Product)

[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, i'm ethan, ae on this account, priya and jonas are our se leads for Optimize. can you do a quick round robin?
[00:12] Maya: sure this is maya, cto at cedar analytics, we run a realtime summarization and routing system for incoming documents, latency under 200ms is kind of our sweet spot.
[00:20] Liam: liam here - ml eng - i'm the one who will run the benchmarks and integrate the sdk.
[00:25] Rosa: rosa - product - mainly focused on quality metrics and regressions.
[00:30] Priya: great, quick agenda — we'll show the Optimize console, walk through quantization profiles (int8 vs fp8), do a live sandbox run, and discuss rollout/fallback rules.

[02:05] Jonas: opening the console now. top left is the project's "Precision Sandbox" environment. i've preloaded cedar-sample-1 prompts and a small model, this is reproducible in your workspace.
[02:33] Maya: quick question, will this be on hosted infra or dedicated? we've got data residency constraints for some PII.
[02:40] Ethan: good q — for the sandbox it'll be hosted but in our customer-dedicated tenant; for production you can choose dedicated or private VPC. we'll share the private deployment checklist if needed.

[04:10] Priya: jumping into Optimize > Profiles. you can see the heatmap — rows are prompts grouped by archetype, columns are precision profiles. darker cells mean higher quality delta vs baseline. right now baseline is FP16.
[04:40] Liam: what's the baseline model? is it the open Llama variant we discussed?
[04:46] Jonas: yes, model is LlamaX-13B-finetuned (labelled as "llx-13b-cd-v2" in the console). kernel selection is automated, and we show per-profile latency medians.

[06:00] Priya: show the int8 profile — you'll notice int8 reduces median token latency by ~28% but some archetypes show quality regression on instruction-following prompts. the console highlights prompt buckets with significant delta and links to sample outputs.
[06:35] Rosa: sample outputs — can you show an example where int8 failed?
[06:40] Jonas: sure — here's prompt #72, a legal-style summarization. fp16 output: "...summary: procedural recommendations..." while int8 output: "...summery: proterd recs..." — transcription note: the tokenizer's numeric rounding surfaced as word-level noise.
[07:10] Maya: that's concerning for legal use cases. how do you detect those automatically?
[07:20] Priya: we do a mix of automated metrics (ROUGE-L, BLEU-ish heuristics, embedding-similarity) and can plug in your human eval set. console flags any prompt where metric delta crosses your threshold. we also show per-token perplexity changes as a proxy.
[08:02] Liam: can we set different thresholds per archetype? e.g., stricter for legal, looser for routing?
[08:09] Priya: absolutely — per-bucket SLOs are supported. you configure quality thresholds and target latency and Optimize recommends the profile that meets constraints or suggests a hybrid rollout.

[10:30] Ethan: let's talk fp8 — fp8 tends to keep quality closer to fp16 while still giving roughly 15-20% latency improvement depending on kernel and sequence length. fp8 also preserves rare token fidelity better than int8.
[10:55] Rosa: so fp8 looks safer for high-stakes prompts but costs a bit more?
[11:00] Jonas: cost here is a function of throughput and GPU memory usage. int8 often allows higher batch sizes which drives down per-token cost, fp8 sits in middle. the console shows estimated per-1M-token cost for each profile based on your workload distribution.

[12:40] Maya: what about fallback rules — can we run int8 in prod but automatically fall back to fp16 when quality drops?
[12:50] Priya: yes, two options — local per-request fallback where the runtime detects a confidence drop and re-runs in higher precision (incurs a latency penalty), or a preemptive routing rule where low-sensitivity archetypes go to int8 and high-sensitivity to fp16/fp8. both are configurable in the console.
[13:30] Liam: re-run sounds expensive, how do you avoid double-billing or excessive latency spikes?
[13:40] Jonas: you can cap max retries and use a sampling strategy (e.g., 1% re-runs) for adaptive monitoring. most customers use hybrid routing rather than full on-the-fly re-run.

[15:00] Priya: demo time — i'm launching a precision sweep across three profiles: fp16 baseline, fp8-s conservative, int8-aggressive. running on a 100-prompt batch from cedar-sample-1. watch the live dashboard.
[15:20] [screen share noise] Jonas: starting benchmark, sending warmup, measure cold and hot latencies, kv-cache hit rates included.
[18:05] Priya: live results populating — int8 median latency 132ms, fp8 160ms, fp16 215ms. quality deltas: int8 average embedding similarity drop 0.06, fp8 drop 0.015. these are aggregated, see per-archetype in the right pane.
[19:30] Rosa: embedding similarity - what metric exactly?
[19:34] Priya: cosine similarity on sentence embeddings (we use Redwood-embed-2 as a default), but you can plug in your own metric or human scores.
[20:10] Liam: for the archetype where int8 failed, how many examples triggered the threshold?
[20:16] Priya: 4 out of 24 for the legal bucket; the console shows example diffs and a diff viewer.

[22:00] Maya: are the profiling artifacts and logs exportable for audits? we need to show SRE and compliance teams.
[22:12] Ethan: yes, audit logs, per-request traces, and the benchmark CSV export are available. we also include model hashes and kernel versions for reproducibility.

[24:05] Jonas: another feature — "Adaptive Precision Rollout" — you can schedule a canary where 10% of traffic autoswitches to int8 for low-risk buckets, monitor, and then increase to 50%/100%. console has pre-built policies for that.
[24:40] Liam: will the canary handle multi-region traffic? we have latency-sensitive users in eu-west.
[24:47] Priya: yes you can scope rollouts by region, tenant, or route. smart routing will fall back to a compatible variant if capacity's constrained.

[27:00] Rosa: security — KMS integration? Key rotation?
[27:05] Ethan: KMS/HSM integrations supported, you can bring your own key, and we support audit trails for KMS operations. we'll also share SOC2 and ISO docs after this call.

[29:20] Maya: our timeline is tight — pilot in dev in 3 weeks, production in 8 weeks. is that feasible?
[29:30] Priya: feasible — typical flow is: sandbox run (2-3 days of sweeps), 2-week pilot, then staged rollout. we can compress steps if we run the assisted benchmark with you.

[31:10] Jonas: quick note about model variants - the console also suggests quantization-aware variants (quantized+recalibrated) that sometimes reduce regressions compared to naive int8. we keep a catalog of Redwood-verified qprofiles.
[32:05] Liam: will that mean additional fine-tuning?
[32:10] Jonas: sometimes a brief calibration pass on a small dataset is enough — it's not full fine-tune but a weight-recalibration step that Optimize can run automatically in the sandbox.

[34:50] Priya: showing the decision matrix view — input your latency SLO (e.g., p50 < 180ms) and quality tolerance and the console ranks profiles by expected cost and rollback risk. you can export the suggested rollout YAML for infra teams.
[36:00] Maya: can infra consume that YAML to apply routes in our private VPC?
[36:06] Ethan: yes, the YAML maps to our routing API; for private deployments we provide a deployable bundle that your infra can apply.

[38:20] Rosa: about monitoring — do you support alerting on metric regressions tied to a prompt set?
[38:28] Priya: yep — you can define eval sets and tie alerts to delta thresholds. we also integrate with PagerDuty and Slack.

[40:10] Liam: curious about cost modeling — the console estimate seems optimistic, how accurate is it?
[40:18] Jonas: estimates are based on per-profile throughput and historical kernel efficiency; we include a confidence band. for pricing we can run a short production-like pass to get real numbers.

[42:00] Priya: security question — data retention in hosted sandboxes?
[42:06] Ethan: sandbox retains data for 30 days by default; we can extend or provide a wipe schedule. for production private deployments you control retention policies.

[44:40] Maya: ok, so practical recommendation: run int8 for routing and transient prompts, use fp8 for summarization, and keep legal on fp16 with fallback to fp8 if cost becomes untenable?
[44:54] Priya: that's a reasonable starting point. i'd suggest the hybrid profile: int8 for low-risk buckets, fp8 for most summarization, fp16 for legal, and an adaptive fallback rule to fp8 before full fp16 re-run to reduce re-run overhead.

[47:30] Ethan: recording a note — we'll include an example rollout plan in the follow-up doc.

[48:00] Priya: launching a small "calibration" job now — this runs weight recalibration for the fp8 profile on 200 samples. should take about 6 minutes.
[54:15] Priya: recalibration done, quality delta improved on the legal bucket from 0.12 to 0.03 embedding drop, so it's now meh acceptable. console recommends fp8-conservative for legal if you accept that delta.
[54:50] Rosa: great — can we have that calibration run applied to our full 500 prompt set in sandbox?
[54:58] Priya: yes i'll queue that as part of the sandbox job we provision.

[56:20] Ethan: let's recap next steps: ethan will share spreadsheet and invite to sandbox; priya will provision workspace and default qprofiles; liam will send representative prompts. schedule follow-up 60m to review sandbox results.
[56:40] Maya: sounds good, thanks all.
[56:45] Liam: quick pricing question — is there a minimum commit for dedicated?
[56:50] Ethan: yes for dedicated we typically require a monthly reserved commit, but we can share options. i'll include pricing tiers in the follow-up.
[57:10] Rosa: can you also include the SOC2 artifact link?
[57:15] Ethan: yes i'll attach SOC2 and ISO docs.
[57:30] [58:00] Meeting ends. Recap email to be sent with artifacts and sandbox invite.
